sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ kṛṣṇā pāṇḍavaṃ pratyupāviśat yudhiṣṭhiraṃ yājñasenī dharmarājaṃ yaśasvinī
english: Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇā, the daughter of Yajñasena, the illustrious one, seated herself before the Pāṇḍava Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvopaviṣṭāṃ rājarṣiḥ pāṇḍavo mahiṣīṃ priyām pratyuvāca sa dharmātmā draupadīṃ cārudarśanām
english: Seeing his beloved queen seated thus, the royal sage, the righteous Pāṇḍava, replied to the fair-faced Draupadī.

sanskrit: dharmyaṃ dharmeṇa dharmajñe prāptās te nidhanaṃ śubhe putrās te bhrātaraś caiva tān na śocitum arhasi
english: O knower of duty, O auspicious one, by righteous means and in keeping with their duty your sons and your brothers have met their death; you ought not to grieve for them.

sanskrit: droṇaputraḥ sa kalyāṇi vanaṃ dūram ito gataḥ tasya tvaṃ pātanaṃ saṃkhye kathaṃ jñāsyasi śobhane
english: O gracious lady, the son of Droṇa has gone far away into the forest; O lovely one, how shall you ever know of his fall in battle?

sanskrit: draupady uvāca droṇaputrasya sahajo maṇiḥ śirasi me śrutaḥ nihatya saṃkhye taṃ pāpaṃ paśyeyaṃ maṇim āhṛtam rājañ śirasi taṃ kṛtvā jīveyam iti me matiḥ
english: Draupadī said: I have heard that the son of Droṇa bears a gem upon his head, born with him. When that wicked one is slain in battle, let me look upon that gem brought to me; my resolve, O king, is to live only after setting it upon your head.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā pāṇḍavaṃ kṛṣṇā rājānaṃ cārudarśanā bhīmasenam athābhyetya kupitā vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to the Pāṇḍava king, the fair-faced Kṛṣṇā then approached Bhīmasena and, in her wrath, addressed these words to him.

sanskrit: trātum arhasi māṃ bhīma kṣatradharmam anusmaran jahi taṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ śambaraṃ maghavān iva na hi te vikrame tulyaḥ pumān astīha kaś cana
english: You must save me, Bhīma, remembering the duty of a warrior; slay that doer of evil as Maghavān slew Śambara. For there is no man here whose valor is the equal of yours.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ tat sarvalokeṣu paramavyasane yathā dvīpo 'bhūs tvaṃ hi pārthānāṃ nagare vāraṇāvate hiḍimbadarśane caiva tathā tvam abhavo gatiḥ
english: It is known in all the worlds how, in their utmost distress, you were an island of refuge to the sons of Pṛthā in the city of Vāraṇāvata; and likewise, when Hiḍimba appeared, you became their deliverance.

sanskrit: tathā virāṭanagare kīcakena bhṛśārditām mām apy uddhṛtavān kṛcchrāt paulomīṃ maghavān iva
english: So too in the city of Virāṭa, when I was sorely tormented by Kīcaka, you raised me up out of that peril, as Maghavān rescued Paulomī.

sanskrit: yathaitāny akṛthāḥ pārtha mahākarmāṇi vai purā tathā drauṇim amitraghna vinihatya sukhī bhava
english: As you accomplished those great deeds of old, O son of Pṛthā, so now, O slayer of foes, strike down the son of Droṇa and find your peace.

sanskrit: tasyā bahuvidhaṃ duḥkhān niśamya paridevitam nāmarṣayata kaunteyo bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ
english: Hearing her manifold lament born of grief, Bhīmasena, the mighty son of Kuntī, could not bear it.

sanskrit: sa kāñcanavicitrāṅgam āruroha mahāratham ādāya ruciraṃ citraṃ samārgaṇaguṇaṃ dhanuḥ
english: He mounted his great chariot, its body wondrously wrought with gold, taking up his bright and splendid bow strung with its bowstring and furnished with arrows.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ sārathiṃ kṛtvā droṇaputravadhe vṛtaḥ visphārya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ tūrṇam aśvān acodayat
english: Making Nakula his charioteer, bent upon the slaying of Droṇa's son, he twanged his arrow-laden bow and swiftly urged on the horses.

sanskrit: te hayāḥ puruṣavyāghra coditā vātaraṃhasaḥ vegena tvaritā jagmur harayaḥ śīghragāminaḥ
english: O tiger among men, those horses, swift as the wind, urged on, sped away with great speed, those tawny coursers fleet of foot.

sanskrit: śibirāt svād gṛhītvā sa rathasya padam acyutaḥ droṇaputrarathasyāśu yayau mārgeṇa vīryavān
english: From his own camp the unshaken, valiant one picked up the track of the chariot and quickly followed the path of the chariot of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin prayāte durdharṣe yadūnām ṛṣabhas tataḥ abravīt puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When that unassailable one had set forth, the bull of the Yadus, the lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, then spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇḍava te bhrātā putraśokam apārayan jighāṃsur drauṇim ākrande yāti bhārata bhārataḥ
english: O Pāṇḍava, O descendant of Bharata, this brother of yours, unable to endure his grief for the slain sons, goes forth with intent to kill, this scion of Bharata's line, into the fray.

sanskrit: bhīmaḥ priyas te sarvebhyo bhrātṛbhyo bharatarṣabha taṃ kṛcchragatam adya tvaṃ kasmān nābhyavapadyase
english: O bull of the Bharatas, Bhīma is dearer to you than all your brothers; why do you not now go to his aid when he is fallen into danger?

sanskrit: yat tad ācaṣṭa putrāya droṇaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ astraṃ brahmaśiro nāma dahed yat pṛthivīm api
english: That weapon which Droṇa, conqueror of hostile cities, taught to his son, the weapon named Brahmaśiras, which could burn up even the earth—

sanskrit: tan mahātmā mahābhāgaḥ ketuḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām pratyapādayad ācāryaḥ prīyamāṇo dhanaṃjayam
english: that the great-souled, illustrious preceptor, the banner of all bowmen, also imparted to Dhanaṃjaya, in his fondness for him.

sanskrit: tatputro 'syaivam evainam anvayācad amarṣaṇaḥ tataḥ provāca putrāya nātihṛṣṭamanā iva
english: His son too, the impatient one, begged the same of him in like manner; and then, with no great gladness of heart, he spoke to his son.

sanskrit: viditaṃ cāpalaṃ hy āsīd ātmajasya mahātmanaḥ sarvadharmavid ācāryo nānviṣat satataṃ sutam
english: For the rashness of his own son was known to that great soul; the preceptor, knower of all duty, did not always approve of his son.

sanskrit: paramāpadgatenāpi na sma tāta tvayā raṇe idam astraṃ prayoktavyaṃ mānuṣeṣu viśeṣataḥ
english: "Even in the gravest peril, my child, this weapon must not be loosed by you in battle, and least of all against human beings."

sanskrit: ity uktavān guruḥ putraṃ droṇaḥ paścād athoktavān na tvaṃ jātu satāṃ mārge sthāteti puruṣarṣabha
english: Having so spoken to his son, the teacher Droṇa added afterward, O bull among men: "You will never abide in the path of the good."

sanskrit: sa tad ājñāya duṣṭātmā pitur vacanam apriyam nirāśaḥ sarvakalyāṇaiḥ śocan paryapatan mahīm
english: Learning his father's unwelcome words, that wicked-souled one, despairing of all good fortune, wandered the earth in grief.

sanskrit: tatas tadā kuruśreṣṭha vanasthe tvayi bhārata avasad dvārakām etya vṛṣṇibhiḥ paramārcitaḥ
english: Then, O best of the Kurus, O descendant of Bharata, while you dwelt in the forest, he came to Dvārakā and lived there, highly honored by the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit samudrānte vasan drāravatīm anu eka ekaṃ samāgamya mām uvāca hasann iva
english: Once, while dwelling by the seashore near Dvāravatī, coming upon me alone and one to one, he said to me, as if smiling:

sanskrit: yat tad ugraṃ tapaḥ kṛṣṇa caran satyaparākramaḥ agastyād bhāratācāryaḥ pratyapadyata me pitā
english: "That fierce austerity which my father, the teacher of the Bharatas, of truthful valor, performed, and through which he obtained from Agastya, O Kṛṣṇa—

sanskrit: astraṃ brahmaśiro nāma devagandharvapūjitam tad adya mayi dāśārha yathā pitari me tathā
english: the weapon named Brahmaśiras, honored by gods and gandharvas—that now resides in me, O scion of the Daśārhas, even as it did in my father.

sanskrit: asmattas tad upādāya divyam astraṃ yadūttama mamāpy astraṃ prayaccha tvaṃ cakraṃ ripuharaṇaṃ raṇe
english: Taking from me that divine weapon, O best of the Yadus, give me in return your weapon, the discus that destroys foes in battle."

sanskrit: sa rājan prīyamāṇena mayāpy uktaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ yācamānaḥ prayatnena matto 'straṃ bharatarṣabha
english: O king, as he begged earnestly of me with joined palms for the weapon, I too, well-pleased, said to him, O bull of the Bharatas:

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvamanuṣyapatagoragāḥ na samā mama vīryasya śatāṃśenāpi piṇḍitāḥ
english: "Gods, demons, gandharvas, men, birds, and serpents, all together, are not equal to even a hundredth part of my strength.

sanskrit: idaṃ dhanur iyaṃ śaktir idaṃ cakram iyaṃ gadā yad yad icchasi ced astraṃ mattas tat tad dadāni te
english: Here is my bow, here my spear, here my discus, here my mace; whatever weapon you desire of me, that I shall give you.

sanskrit: yac chaknoṣi samudyantuṃ prayoktum api vā raṇe tad gṛhāṇa vināstreṇa yan me dātum abhīpsasi
english: Whatever you are able to lift up and to wield in battle, take that—without giving me a weapon in exchange, that which you wish to bestow on me."

sanskrit: sa sunābhaṃ sahasrāraṃ vajranābham ayasmayam vavre cakraṃ mahābāho spardhamāno mayā saha
english: O mighty-armed one, he chose the discus with its fair nave, its thousand spokes, its adamantine hub, wrought of iron, vying thus with me.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇa cakram ity ukto mayā tu tadanantaram jagrāhopetya sahasā cakraṃ savyena pāṇinā na caitad aśakat sthānāt saṃcālayitum acyuta
english: "Take the discus," I said; and thereupon, approaching, he suddenly seized the discus with his left hand, but he was unable, O unfailing one, to stir it from its place.

sanskrit: atha tad dakṣiṇenāpi grahītum upacakrame sarvayatnena tenāpi gṛhṇann etad akalpayat
english: Then he set himself to grasp it with his right hand as well, and though seizing it with his whole effort, he could not make it move.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvabalenāpi yac caitan na śaśāka saḥ uddhartuṃ vā cālayituṃ drauṇiḥ paramadurmanāḥ kṛtvā yatnaṃ paraṃ śrāntaḥ sa nyavartata bhārata
english: Then, when even with all his might the son of Droṇa could neither lift nor shift it, O descendant of Bharata, deeply downcast and wearied after his utmost striving, he gave up.

sanskrit: nivṛttam atha taṃ tasmād abhiprāyād vicetasam aham āmantrya susnigdham aśvatthāmānam abruvam
english: When Aśvatthāman had thus turned back from that purpose, bewildered, I called to him most tenderly and said:

sanskrit: yaḥ sa devamanuṣyeṣu pramāṇaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ gāṇḍīvadhanvā śvetāśvaḥ kapipravaraketanaḥ
english: "He who among gods and men has attained the highest measure, the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, of the white horses, bearing the banner of the chief of apes—

sanskrit: yaḥ sākṣād devadeveśaṃ śitikaṇṭham umāpatim dvaṃdvayuddhe parājiṣṇus toṣayām āsa śaṃkaram
english: he who, victorious in single combat, gratified the very lord of the lords of gods, the blue-throated husband of Umā, Śaṃkara—

sanskrit: yasmāt priyataro nāsti mamānyaḥ puruṣo bhuvi nādeyaṃ yasya me kiṃ cid api dārāḥ sutās tathā
english: than whom there is no other man dearer to me on earth, to whom there is nothing of mine I would withhold—not my wife, not my sons—

sanskrit: tenāpi suhṛdā brahman pārthenākliṣṭakarmaṇā noktapurvam idaṃ vākyaṃ yat tvaṃ mām abhibhāṣase
english: even by that friend, O brāhmaṇa, the son of Pṛthā of untiring deeds, these words which you now speak to me have never before been uttered.

sanskrit: brahmacaryaṃ mahad ghoraṃ cīrtvā dvādaśavārṣikam himavatpārśvam abhyetya yo mayā tapasārcitaḥ
english: He who, having kept a great and terrible vow of celibacy for twelve years, was won by me through austerity upon the slopes of the Himālaya—

sanskrit: samānavratacāriṇyāṃ rukmiṇyāṃ yo 'nvajāyata sanatkumāras tejasvī pradyumno nāma me sutaḥ
english: my radiant son named Pradyumna, who was born of Rukmiṇī, the partner of my equal vow, and who is Sanatkumāra himself—

sanskrit: tenāpy etan mahad divyaṃ cakram apratimaṃ mama na prārthitam abhūn mūḍha yad idaṃ prārthitaṃ tvayā
english: even by him this great and matchless divine discus of mine was never asked for, O foolish one—that which you have asked of me.

sanskrit: rāmeṇātibalenaitan noktapūrvaṃ kadā cana na gadena na sāmbena yad idaṃ prārthitaṃ tvayā
english: Never before has this been asked by the exceedingly mighty Rāma, nor by Gada, nor by Sāmba—that which you have asked of me.

sanskrit: dvārakāvāsibhiś cānyair vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathaiḥ noktapūrvam idaṃ jātu yad idaṃ prārthitaṃ tvayā
english: Nor by the other dwellers of Dvārakā, the great chariot-warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas, has this ever been asked—that which you have asked of me.

sanskrit: bhāratācāryaputraḥ san mānitaḥ sarvayādavaiḥ cakreṇa rathināṃ śreṣṭha kiṃ nu tāta yuyutsase
english: Being the son of the teacher of the Bharatas and honored by all the Yādavas, with this discus, O best of chariot-warriors, against whom, my child, do you wish to make war?"

sanskrit: evam ukto mayā drauṇir mām idaṃ pratyuvāca ha prayujya bhavate pūjāṃ yotsye kṛṣṇa tvayety uta
english: Thus addressed by me, the son of Droṇa answered me in these words: "Having offered you homage, I shall fight with you, O Kṛṣṇa."

sanskrit: tatas te prārthitaṃ cakraṃ devadānavapūjitam ajeyaḥ syām iti vibho satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "It was therefore that I sought your discus, honored by gods and demons, thinking, 'May I become invincible.' This truth I tell you, O lord.

sanskrit: tvatto 'haṃ durlabhaṃ kāmam anavāpyaiva keśava pratiyāsyāmi govinda śivenābhivadasva mām
english: Without having gained from you this desire so hard to win, O Keśava, I shall depart; speak to me kindly, O Govinda.

sanskrit: etat sunābhaṃ vṛṣṇīnām ṛṣabheṇa tvayā dhṛtam cakram apraticakreṇa bhuvi nānyo 'bhipadyate
english: This fair-naved discus, borne by you, the bull of the Vṛṣṇis, against whom no other discus can prevail—none other on earth may attain it."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā drauṇir māṃ yugyam aśvān dhanāni ca ādāyopayayau bālo ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: Having said only this much to me, the youth, the son of Droṇa, took a team of horses, riches, and jewels of many kinds, and went away.

sanskrit: sa saṃrambhī durātmā ca capalaḥ krūra eva ca veda cāstraṃ brahmaśiras tasmād rakṣyo vṛkodaraḥ
english: He is wrathful and evil-souled, fickle and cruel, and he knows the Brahmaśiras weapon; therefore Vṛkodara must be guarded.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvayādavanandanaḥ sarvāyudhavaropetam āruroha mahāratham yuktaṃ paramakāmbojais turagair hemamālibhiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the best of warriors, the delight of all the Yādavas, mounted his great chariot furnished with the finest of all weapons, yoked with splendid Kāmboja steeds adorned with golden garlands.

sanskrit: ādityodayavarṇasya dhuraṃ rathavarasya tu dakṣiṇām avahat sainyaḥ sugrīvaḥ savyato 'vahat pārṣṇivāhau tu tasyāstāṃ meghapuṣpabalāhakau
english: Of that excellent chariot, hued like the rising sun, Sainya bore the right side of the yoke and Sugrīva bore the left; and Meghapuṣpa and Balāhaka were its two flanking steeds at the rear.

sanskrit: viśvakarmakṛtā divyā nānāratnavibhūṣitā ucchriteva rathe māyā dhvajayaṣṭir adṛśyata
english: The flagstaff, divine, wrought by Viśvakarman, adorned with jewels of many kinds, raised aloft upon the chariot, appeared like very magic.

sanskrit: vainateyaḥ sthitas tasyāṃ prabhāmaṇḍalaraśmivān tasya satyavataḥ ketur bhujagārir adṛśyata
english: Upon it stood the son of Vinatā, ringed with a halo of radiant beams; the foe of serpents appeared as the banner of that truthful one.

sanskrit: anvārohad dhṛṣīkeśaḥ ketuḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām arjunaḥ satyakarmā ca kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Hṛṣīkeśa mounted, and after him the banner of all bowmen, Arjuna of truthful deeds, and Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of the Kurus.

sanskrit: aśobhetāṃ mahātmānau dāśārham abhitaḥ sthitau rathasthaṃ śārṅgadhanvānam aśvināv iva vāsavam
english: The two great souls, standing on either side of the scion of the Daśārhas, shone forth beside the wielder of Śārṅga seated in the chariot, like the two Aśvins beside Vāsava.

sanskrit: tāv upāropya dāśārhaḥ syandanaṃ lokapūjitam pratodena javopetān paramāśvān acodayat
english: Having taken the two up into the world-honored chariot, the scion of the Daśārhas, with his goad, urged on the swift and excellent steeds.

sanskrit: te hayāḥ sahasotpetur gṛhītvā syandanottamam āsthitaṃ pāṇḍaveyābhyāṃ yadūnām ṛṣabheṇa ca
english: Those horses suddenly sprang forward, bearing away that finest of chariots mounted by the two Pāṇḍavas and by the bull of the Yadus.

sanskrit: vahatāṃ śārṅgadhanvānam aśvānāṃ śīghragāminām prādurāsīn mahāñ śabdaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ patatām iva
english: From the swift-going horses that bore the wielder of Śārṅga there arose a great sound, like that of birds in flight.

sanskrit: te samārchan naravyāghrāḥ kṣaṇena bharatarṣabha bhīmasenaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ samanudrutya vegitāḥ
english: Those tigers among men, O bull of the Bharatas, swiftly pursuing, overtook in a moment the great bowman Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: krodhadīptaṃ tu kaunteyaṃ dviṣadarthe samudyatam nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ sametyāpi mahārathāḥ
english: But the son of Kuntī, blazing with wrath and bent upon his enemy's destruction, even those great chariot-warriors, though they came up with him, could not turn back.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ prekṣatām eva śrīmatāṃ dṛḍhadhanvinām yayau bhāgirathīkacchaṃ haribhir bhṛśavegitaiḥ yatra sma śrūyate drauṇiḥ putrahantā mahātmanām
english: Before the very eyes of those illustrious and firm-bowed ones, he sped with his fleet horses to the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, where the son of Droṇa, slayer of the sons of the great-souled ones, was said to be.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahātmānam udakānte yaśasvinam kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ vyāsam āsīnam ṛṣibhiḥ saha
english: He beheld the great and illustrious soul, Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana Vyāsa, seated at the water's edge together with the sages.

sanskrit: taṃ caiva krūrakarmāṇaṃ ghṛtāktaṃ kuśacīriṇam rajasā dhvastakeśāntaṃ dadarśa drauṇim antike
english: And nearby he saw that doer of cruel deeds, the son of Droṇa, smeared with ghee, clad in garments of kuśa grass, his hair-ends grimed with dust.

sanskrit: tam abhyadhāvat kaunteyaḥ pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ bhīmaseno mahābāhus tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: The mighty-armed Bhīmasena, son of Kuntī, rushed upon him, taking up his arrow-laden bow, and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā bhīmadhanvānaṃ pragṛhītaśarāsanam bhrātarau pṛṣṭhataś cāsya janārdanarathe sthitau vyathitātmābhavad drauṇiḥ prāptaṃ cedam amanyata
english: Seeing the terrible bowman with his bow drawn, and his two brothers standing behind him in Janārdana's chariot, the son of Droṇa grew troubled at heart and thought his hour had come.

sanskrit: sa tad divyam adīnātmā paramāstram acintayat jagrāha ca sa caiṣīkāṃ drauṇiḥ savyena pāṇinā sa tām āpadam āsādya divyam astram udīrayat
english: Undaunted in spirit, he called to mind that divine, supreme weapon; and the son of Droṇa took up a blade of reed-grass in his left hand and, fallen into that extremity, charged it with the divine weapon.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇas tāñ śūrān divyāyudhadharān sthitān apāṇḍavāyeti ruṣā vyasṛjad dāruṇaṃ vacaḥ
english: Unable to endure those heroes standing armed with divine weapons, in his wrath he loosed the terrible utterance: "For the destruction of the Pāṇḍavas!"

sanskrit: ity uktvā rājaśārdūla droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān sarvalokapramohārthaṃ tad astraṃ pramumoca ha
english: Having so spoken, O tiger among kings, the valiant son of Droṇa loosed that weapon for the confounding of all the worlds.

sanskrit: tatas tasyām iṣīkāyāṃ pāvakaḥ samajāyata pradhakṣyann iva lokāṃs trīn kālāntakayamopamaḥ
english: Then from that reed-blade a fire arose, as if to consume the three worlds, like Yama who brings the end at the close of time.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca iṅgitenaiva dāśārhas tam abhiprāyam āditaḥ drauṇer buddhvā mahābāhur arjunaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Discerning from the outset, by his very gesture, the intent of the son of Droṇa, the mighty-armed scion of the Daśārhas spoke to Arjuna.

sanskrit: arjunārjuna yad divyam astraṃ te hṛdi vartate droṇopadiṣṭaṃ tasyāyaṃ kālaḥ saṃprati pāṇḍava
english: "Arjuna, Arjuna! That divine weapon which abides in your heart, taught to you by Droṇa—now is its time, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇām ātmanaś caiva paritrāṇāya bhārata visṛjaitat tvam apy ājāv astram astranivāraṇam
english: For the deliverance of your brothers and of yourself, O descendant of Bharata, do you too loose in this fray that weapon which wards off weapons."

sanskrit: keśavenaivam uktas tu pāṇḍavaḥ paravīrahā avātarad rathāt tūrṇaṃ pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Thus addressed by Keśava, the Pāṇḍava, slayer of enemy heroes, swiftly descended from the chariot, taking up his arrow-laden bow.

sanskrit: pūrvam ācāryaputrāya tato 'nantaram ātmane bhrātṛbhyaś caiva sarvebhyaḥ svastīty uktvā paraṃtapaḥ
english: First for the son of his teacher, then thereafter for himself and for all his brothers, the scorcher of foes uttered the words "May it be well."
